Messages.Author: John Whelan
Messages.Body:
Greetings LSJ

Our playgroup recently had a disagreement which we need resolved by
Authority.

Player A bleeds for one.
Player B declares that he is taking the bleed and removes pool
Player A plays conditioning
Player B plays deflection

At this point two conflicting points of view are presented:

1) Player B already declared that he was taking the bleed, and should be
held to that. He may not play deflection.

2) Player B's failure to block is the only part of his decision that is
final. Otherwise he has the right to respond to any new effects
presented. He may deflect the bleed.

Thank you in advance.

-- John Whelan

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
John Whelan wrote:
> Player A bleeds for one.
> Player B declares that he is taking the bleed and removes pool
> Player A plays conditioning
> Player B plays deflection
>
> At this point two conflicting points of view are presented:
>
> 1) Player B already declared that he was taking the bleed, and should be
> held to that. He may not play deflection.
>
> 2) Player B's failure to block is the only part of his decision that is
> final. Otherwise he has the right to respond to any new effects
> presented. He may deflect the bleed.

2) is correct.
After declaring "no block" (which is all that "I'll take it" can mean at this
point), the acting Methuselah gets first opportunity to play an effect - she
chooses to play Conditioning. The she gets the opportunity to play the next
effect. Sh chooses to play no further effects, so the target Methuselah gets
the opportunity to play an effect - she chooses to play Deflection. After
this event, the acting Methuselah again gets the opportunity to play the
next effect, and so on.

See "Sequencing" in the rulebook. [1.6.1.5]
